headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can leak warehouse data into a prompt-injection-prone downstream workflow, while direct capability conflict is limited by B's no-egress profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can read and transform warehouse data, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage. If dbt outputs are copied into B or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled text in data can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented isolation, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs are copied into system_prompts_leaks inputs via a shared file or clipboard, injection is plausible.
IF warehouse rows contain adversarial text and B parses them as instructions, prompt hijack risk materializes.
mitigations: Use a manual review step before B consumes any dbt-generated text.
Strip or escape instruction-like tokens from dbt outputs.
Keep dbt artifacts and B inputs in separate directories.
Disable copy-paste transfer of raw model output between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, so sensitive warehouse content can leave its boundary. system_prompts_leaks has no declared data classes or egress, but its purpose suggests prompt-content handling; the pairwise leakage path is indirect yet plausible. With no shared-workspace evidence, this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF dbt-core processes sensitive warehouse tables and exports derived text to B, leakage occurs.
IF B is used to inspect or summarize dbt artifacts, those artifacts may be exposed outside the warehouse boundary.
mitigations: Limit dbt runs to non-sensitive schemas.
Redact sensitive columns before any handoff to B.
Review allowlisted egress destinations for dbt-core.
Keep B offline from warehouse exports unless explicitly approved.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: dbt-core has allowlisted network egress and API access to a data warehouse, while system_prompts_leaks shows no write, network, or OAuth scopes. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty is low because B exposes no conflicting write surface.
conditions: IF B is later given write access to the same warehouse or repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not shown in either profile, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Avoid granting both agents write access to the same warehouse objects.
Document any shared mutable resources before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core produces transformation outputs that B could render or summarize, and system_prompts_leaks is centered on prompt leakage rather than verification. If B treats dbt output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream reports. The pair lacks evidence of a built-in verification step, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes dbt-generated metrics or narratives without validation, cascading error occurs.
IF dbt model changes are propagated to B outputs automatically, stale or wrong facts can be amplified.
mitigations: Require B to cite source tables for every claim.
Add a checksum or version check on dbt artifacts.
Insert a human review step before downstream publication.
Compare B outputs against warehouse queries for critical metrics.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which may include regulated data classes, while system_prompts_leaks has no stated residency, retention, or certification controls. Because the pair could move warehouse data into a separate source-available project context, compliance mismatch is plausible. The other agent lacks explicit compliance fields, so I cannot justify high.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated records and B stores or logs them, retention/residency mismatch occurs.
IF organizational policy requires certified handling for warehouse data, B may violate it.
mitigations: Classify warehouse tables before any handoff.
Do not export regulated rows into B workflows.
Check retention and logging settings for both tools.
Use a separate environment for regulated datasets.
